content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Start digital

Current payment platforms can be restrictive and often exclude markets like Kenya, where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable. This poses a challenge for creators who want to sell digital products without compromise. COREMERCH's infrastructure offers an alternative that's built on ownership, control, and reliability. Unlike traditional platforms that hold your funds, this commerce stack ensures that you retain full control over your payment processing, data, and digital goods. The architecture is designed to bypass the limitations of conventional systems, allowing you to accept payments in cryptocurrency while benefiting from low fees and immediate transaction confirmation. This new model eliminates dependence on third-party platforms, fostering a truly sovereign commerce environment.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before launching your online store, gather essential resources. First, collect your digital products—ebooks, courses, or templates—that you plan to sell. Next, ensure you have a domain name for your store. Choose a reliable hosting service like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages to host your site at no cost. Familiarize yourself with Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers, as these will manage your backend logic and automate delivery. You’ll also need to set up a crypto wallet to process payments via NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies. Lastly, acquire the Complete Builder Kit to simplify your setup. This kit provides comprehensive documentation and all necessary templates to ensure your deployment is seamless.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Establishing an efficient payment and delivery pipeline is critical for your digital store. Start by integrating NOWPayments for crypto payment processing. This platform allows you to accept transactions in various cryptocurrencies, automatically converting prices to USD at the time of the sale. Configure your Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers to handle transaction confirmations and trigger product delivery. Use Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for hosting your digital files, ensuring that they are accessible post-purchase. Implement webhook notifications to automate delivery when payments are confirmed on-chain. This setup ensures that customers receive their products immediately after payment, enhancing their shopping experience and building trust in your brand.
Empower your creativity with full control over your sales.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After setting up your infrastructure, it's time to go live. Begin by thoroughly testing your payment and delivery pipeline. Create test products and perform transactions to ensure everything is functioning as expected. Once satisfied, officially launch your store by promoting it through social media channels and online communities. Make sure to communicate how customers can purchase through cryptocurrency, emphasizing the convenience and security of your payment system. Monitor the first few transactions closely to address any issues quickly. With immediate feedback from customers, you can refine your process, ensuring a smooth experience for future buyers.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your store is operational, consider strategies for scaling. Start by analyzing customer feedback and transaction data to identify popular products and areas for improvement. Invest in SEO to increase your store's visibility and attract more users. Expand your product range by creating new digital items or bundling existing products. Leverage social media marketing to reach a wider audience and engage with potential customers. Collaborating with other creators or influencers can also enhance your reach. Keep an eye on your infrastructure performance, ensuring that it can handle increased traffic and transactions as your business grows.
